THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE 165

Mr. Ashcraft taught school at at Polytechnic College as Professor of Higher Mathematics, Natural Science, and Education, and at Savoy Male and Female College lege as a teacher, but had a brief interlude in his progress toward his lifework. Like Professor Pritchett and Holland, he was his only as 'Pink' Montgomery, not having been in school with him. Mr. Ashcraft came to Texas at an early age. He graduated from Polytechnic, and in 1883 he graduated with honors at Vanderbilt University. He commenced his course of studies by reading with Dr. I. S. King in Louisville, in 1887, the subject spent a portion of the school with the students there. He graduated from a four-year medical course at Louisville, in 1879, graduating in 1880.

He was married on December 16, 1885, to Miss Aggie McKee, now of Ralls, Texas, early settler, formerly of Bonham, Texasa[?]. For his later history, see footnote:*

From the Baptist News, founded in December, 1886, at Honey Grove, it is learned that after the destruction of Savoy College, Professor Pritchett then took up the study of law and was admitted to the bar of Texas, and at Bonham Daily Favorite, College, Bonham.

Mr. Pritchett served for many years as steward and Sunday School superintendent at Bonham, and was a member of the Methodist Episcopal Church.

He was a member of the Knights of Pythias, and a Mason, and a deacon in the church, and a very prominent member in the community. He was prominent in the councils of the Anti-Cotton Mill, President for the Artisan Cotton Mills, and had an additional attraction to his public career.

He was prominent in the councils of the Artisan Cotton Mills. He was prominent in the councils of the Anti-Artisan Cotton Mills, and had a very profitable business, known as the Fannie County Abstract.

Mr. Pritchett was foremost in the industrial development of his community through improvements in the Tennessee River at Muscle Shoals.
